blog.title: SEO for Contractors and Plumbers: How to Get the Calls Instead of the Directory
blog.title_tag: SEO for Contractors & Plumbers: What Works | ART3RY
blog.meta_description: SEO for contractors and plumbers, in the order that gets the phone ringing: Google Business Profile, service-area pages, reviews, and speed on the call.
blog.dek: Most contractor SEO advice is written for agencies. This is the short version for someone with a truck, a crew and no time: what to fix first, what to skip, and why the call matters as much as the ranking.

sections.h2: Where contractor customers actually come from
paragraphs: Someone's water heater fails, a breaker keeps tripping, the AC quits in July. They pick up a phone and search a short phrase with a city in it, then call one of the first few businesses they see. Those first few are usually the map results, not the website results underneath.

That is why SEO for a contractor is mostly local SEO. You are not trying to rank for the whole country. You are trying to be one of three names on a map and a list for the towns you actually drive to.

sections.h2: Step one: the Google Business Profile
paragraphs: Start here because it moves the map results fastest and costs nothing but time. Claim and verify the profile, pick the one primary category that matches your main money job (not the broadest one), and add the secondary categories you really do. A plumber who also does water heaters and drain cleaning should say so in the categories and services, not leave it blank.

Fill in every field: hours, service area, phone, website, photos of real work and your real truck. Keep the business name exactly what is on your sign and invoice. Stuffing keywords into the name is against Google's rules and is a common reason profiles get suspended. If your profile is missing or stuck, work through [why a business is not showing up on Google](/blog/why-is-my-business-not-showing-up-on-google/) before anything else.

sections.h2: Step two: one page per service and per town
paragraphs: A single Services page cannot rank for water heater repair, drain cleaning, panel upgrades and AC repair in six towns. Search engines match a page to a search, so give each job you want its own page, and give your biggest towns their own page too, with real content: the work you do there, the neighborhoods, a photo or two, the number to call.

The trap is copying the same page and swapping the city name. Pages like that tend to get ignored. Write each one so it would be useful to a homeowner in that town on its own. I cover the method in [service area pages that rank](/blog/service-area-pages-that-rank/).

sections.h2: Step three: reviews, asked for on the day
paragraphs: Reviews influence both the map ranking and whether a stranger picks you. The reliable method is boring: ask the same day, by text, with a direct link, while the customer is still happy about the fix. Waiting a week cuts the response rate sharply. Reply to every review, including the bad ones, calmly and without arguing. There is a full walkthrough in [how to get more Google reviews](/blog/how-to-get-more-google-reviews/).

sections.h2: The part SEO advice skips: the call itself
paragraphs: You can win the ranking and still lose the job. A contractor on a ladder or under a sink cannot answer, the call goes to voicemail, and the caller moves down the list to the next number. Plenty of people will not leave a message for a trade they have never used.

So the ranking work only pays if the phone is answered. That means either a person who picks up or an assistant that answers, takes the details and texts them to you. If you want the numbers on that, see [missed call lead capture for the trades](/blog/missed-call-lead-capture/) and [what an AI receptionist is](/blog/what-is-an-ai-receptionist/).

Skip buying links from vendors who email you, skip posting the same text to dozens of directories you have never heard of, and skip any promise of a guaranteed number one ranking. Nobody outside Google can guarantee that. A correct profile, real service pages, steady reviews and a phone that gets answered will do more than any of it.
If you want a read on which of these is weakest for your business right now, the [free diagnostic](/diagnostic/) looks at exactly that.

faq.q: How long does SEO take for a contractor?
faq.a: Profile and review fixes can move map results within weeks. New service and town pages usually take a few months to settle. Nobody can promise an exact timeline, because it depends on your area and your competitors.

faq.q: Do I need a website to show up on Google Maps?
faq.a: A verified Google Business Profile can appear without one, but a site with real service and town pages gives you far more searches to appear for and gives callers a reason to trust you.

faq.q: Is SEO or Google Ads better for a plumber?
faq.a: Ads buy calls today and stop when you stop paying. SEO takes longer and keeps working. Many contractors use ads to cover the gap while the profile and pages build.

faq.q: What is the first thing I should fix?
faq.a: Your Google Business Profile: verified, the right primary category, accurate hours and service area, and real photos. Then make sure the phone gets answered.

blog.title: Answering Service for Plumbers, HVAC and Electricians: What to Look For
blog.title_tag: Answering Service for Trades: What to Look For | ART3RY
blog.meta_description: Choosing an answering service for plumbers, HVAC or electricians: emergency triage, job-ready details, text delivery, and the pricing traps to check first.
blog.dek: A trades answering service is judged on one thing: whether the caller ends up as a booked job or a lost one. Here is what separates a service that does that from one that just takes messages.

paragraphs: A dentist's front desk can call a patient back after lunch. A homeowner with water coming through the ceiling cannot wait until you are out from under a house. The caller who reaches voicemail on a trade number usually tries the next number, and the first business to actually talk to them tends to get the job.
That makes the answering service part of how you win work, not an overhead line. The questions below are how to tell a good one from a message-taker.

sections.h2: Does it triage emergencies from routine calls?
paragraphs: Ask how it tells a burst pipe, a no-heat call or a sparking outlet from a quote request. The right setup asks two or three questions, flags the urgent ones and pushes them to you immediately, while the routine ones wait in a clean queue for the morning.
If every call arrives as the same flat message, you will end up checking all of them at 2 AM or ignoring all of them.

You want the name, the number confirmed back to the caller, the address or at least the town, what is wrong in their words, and how soon they need someone. If you have to call back and ask those questions again, the service saved you nothing. I break down the six fields worth capturing in [AI phone intake](/blog/ai-phone-intake/).

A text with the details beats a voicemail you have to listen to between jobs. Ask what happens when you do not respond: does it try a second number, or tell the caller you will call within a stated time? Callers forgive a short wait when they are told about it. They do not forgive silence.

Human services answer in a person's voice and charge for it, usually by the minute or the call. AI services answer instantly at any hour and cost less, but need to be set up to handle your trade's questions properly. Hybrids route between the two. Each has a place, and [virtual receptionist companies compared](/blog/virtual-receptionist-companies-compared/) goes through where each one works and where it breaks.

sections.h2: Check the pricing before you sign
paragraphs: Per-minute billing, per-call billing, minimum monthly fees and charges for after-hours or transfers can make the real monthly cost very different from the advertised rate. Ask for the bill of a customer with your call volume. The detail is in [answering service pricing](/blog/answering-service-pricing/), and the comparison against a hire is in [AI receptionist cost vs a front-desk hire](/blog/ai-receptionist-cost-vs-front-desk-hire/).

I build and run an AI phone assistant for trades that answers every call, asks the right questions, and texts you the job details. If you want to see what it would catch on your own line, start with [never lose a job to voicemail](/never-lose-a-job-to-voicemail/) or the [free diagnostic](/diagnostic/).

faq.q: Do plumbers really need an answering service?
faq.a: If you are often on a job and cannot pick up, yes. Callers with an urgent problem usually call the next business when they reach voicemail.

faq.q: What should an HVAC answering service ask the caller?
faq.a: Name, confirmed phone number, address or town, the problem in their words (no heat, no cooling, noise, leak), how urgent it is, and the best time to reach them.

faq.q: Is an AI answering service good enough for electricians?
faq.a: For intake and booking, yes when it is set up for your trade. Urgent safety calls should be flagged and sent to you right away.

faq.q: How much does an answering service cost?
faq.a: It varies widely by billing method and call volume. Ask for a sample bill at your volume and check for minimums and after-hours fees before you sign.
